# Review — cid-tiradas-78-82 (tiradas 78–82, lines 1287–1384)

Adversarial review against the pinned packet, Pidal's rubrics and footnotes on the scan (PDF pp. 216–223 read at
130 dpi, with crops at 600 dpi and 1200 dpi of Albar/Álbar at vv. 1297, 1302, 1309 against the unaccented A of
Alfonsso v. 1311 and A este v. 1303, of Merced v. 1321, saldríen v. 1353 and aqui v. 1335), conventions.md, the
pilot (01-04) and the published parts (15-17, 18-18, 19-23, 24-26, 44-48, 64-68, 69-74, 75-77 in particular), the
shared glossary and known-forms.json. All edits made by script (json load/dump, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1). No
`t` changed: the 98 `t` lines concatenated equal the packet's 98 verses in order exactly, checked by script after
the edits; one `l` line per `t` line in all 35 units; no unit crosses a tirada.

Checked and found sound (no change):
- Rubrics against the scan, all five right: 78 Don Jerónimo llega a Valencia (p. 212); 79 Don Jerónimo hecho obispo
  (p. 213); 80 Minaya se dirige a Carrión (p. 214); 81 Minaya saluda al rey (p. 215); 82 Discurso de Minaya al
  rey.—Envidia de Garci Ordóñez.—El rey perdona a la familia del Cid.—Los infantes de Carrión codician las riquezas
  del Cid (p. 215). Assonances re-derived: 78 á-o; 79 í-o; 80 á (Fáñez counting); 81 ó-o (apu[o]sto, pu[o]blo,
  du[o]lo); 82 ó with ó-e endings (nombre, corredores, Ordóñez, omne, f[o]ren). Right in all five first notes.
- Footnotes against the scan, wording and verse numbers right: 1288 (coronado 'clérigo', comp. 1501; ex orientis
  partibus / ab Eois partibus, vague phrases for monks and priests from north of the Ebro; inexact for a French
  cleric such as Jerónimo — Pidal's "p. 17" not carried, harmless), 1290 (acordado 'que obra con acuerdo y madurez;
  cuerdo, prudente'), 1295 (cristianos 'nadie', v. 29), 1302 (the Cid makes the bishop de su mano, 1332; kings
  created sees; Urban II and Bernardo of Toledo consecrate; charter of 1098 — the middle of the note, the Toledo
  canon and the 1088 primacy, summarised away, harmless), 1312 (Sahagún 35 km west of Carrión, camino francés o de
  Santiago; Benedictine monastery; devotion from Fernando I; habit 1072; flight to Toledo; burial), 1315
  (presentaja 'presente, regalo'), 1322 and 1338 ('os pide que', 'os pide que los toméis', v. 179), 1329
  (Castejón = Castellón de la Plana, formerly de Burriana; stands for the tierras de Borriana of 1093), 1333 (only
  two of the five battles told), 1342 (Isidore bishop of Seville 599–636; vv. 1867, 3028, 3140; Fernando I moved
  the body to León 1063; sant Esidro el de León 3509), 1343 ('las hazañas que hace'), 1345 (p. 21; the king's

  the note at 1372. "so may the Creator keep you" (v. 1324) matches 44-48.
- `l` ↔ `i` unit by unit: no remembered English found; sense and force agree.

Findings refused:
- 1327–30 `i` "Castellón" for Castejón: a modern name in `i`, as 64-68 gives Almenara for Almenar; the note gives
  Pidal's identification, and the other Castejón (19-23) is a different place, so the modern name helps. Left.
- 1321–24 `l` "so you may-avail the Creator" (sí vos vala el Criador): the word order of `t` kept, as 44-48 does
  ("so you may-protect God"). Left.
- 1303 `i` "they gave him a see in Valencia": "a see" is supplied; the note says what was given is not stated.
  Light interpretation. Left.
- 1292 `i` "He had gone about seeking word": pluperfect for the imperfect andava; he has come from afar, so the
  English past-of-the-past reads naturally. Left.
- 1376 note "Pidal reads it in that inequality of birth": Pidal's note is on v. 1376 and does not speak of
  'daring'; but the note links them reasonably and says the lines leave it unsaid. Left.

Findings refused:
- fagunt "San Facundo", ordóñez "son of Ordoño", fora "Latin fuerat", miyor / mijor "Latin melior": etymologies
  not in Pidal's notes here, but certain. Kept.
- medina "the frontier town on the Jalón": geography beyond Pidal's note, but plain fact and harmless. Kept.
- carrión "Carrión de los Condes": the modern name; Pidal's note to 1376 calls it a city, head of a county. Kept.
- duolo "no relation to modern duelo 'duel'": modern duelo 'grief' survives too, but the entry gives = duelo, pena
  first. Kept.
- prestar: a broaden for 'to benefit, do good to' (prestar nos quiere) was considered; the known 'to be worth,
  avail' covers it. Not added.

## Readings left uncertain

- v. 1287 En estas nuevas: what news is meant; no note.
- v. 1294–95 the force of the clause: that once he had his fill of fighting, no one should ever mourn him.
- v. 1304 diéronle: what was given (the see, its endowment) is not said.
- v. 1306 señor avie obispo: impersonal 'there was' or 'had'.
- v. 1322 Besávavos: why the imperfect, where 1338 has the present.
- v. 1326 faze lo so: 'does his part', exact nuance.
- v. 1327 ganada a Xérica: participle with auxiliary understood, or absolute.
- v. 1335 las señas: 'tokens, proof'; no note.
- v. 1355–59 the italic final e: read as the paragogic e that Pidal names at v. 1385.
- v. 1356, 1358 f[o]ren: 'be' (ser) most likely; 'go' possible.
- v. 1371 otra des[amor]: Pidal's restoration and the sense of the line; no note.
- v. 1375 why the Infantes 'would not dare'; Pidal's note on 1376 bears on it only indirectly.

## Text observations for the establishing run (no `t` changed)

- v. 1309 "Minaya Álbar Fáñez": the drafter suspected Pidal prints Albar unaccented here. At 600 and 1200 dpi the
  capital A of this Álbar has the same shape as the accented Álbar of v. 1302 (apex standing clearly above the l
  ascender, with a flag-like thickening where the accent has fused with the apex), and differs from the unaccented
  A of Alfonsso v. 1311 and A este v. 1303 (apex below the l, symmetric, no flag). Pidal prints Álbar at v. 1309;
  the pinned text is right.
- v. 1297 "Oíd, Minaya Albar Fáñez": pinned unaccented, but on the same crops this A has the accented shape too
  (apex well above the l, with the fused accent), so Pidal most likely prints Álbar here. The establishing run
  should look again; `t` and `l` left as pinned.
- v. 1321 "Merçed, señor Alfonsso": at 600 dpi the c of Merced has no cedilla (its foot sits on the line like the
  e's; compare merçed with cedilla at v. 1351). Pidal prints Merced here; the pinned Merçed looks like a
  normalisation. For the establishing run; `t` not changed (the note's lemma 'Merçed' would then read Merced).
- v. 1353 saldríen: the accent on the i is there (600 dpi); pinned text right.
